trajectories.title: A better router, one question at a time.
trajectories.summary: Retrieved depth weighting becomes a lasting part of the router, even as later searches repeatedly miss the needed implementation.
trajectories.takeaway: Exponential depth weighting introduced at iteration 5 remains in every later best program. At iteration 77, progress occurs despite a retrieval with no promising document.

trajectories.title: From radar codes to a mathematical bound.
trajectories.summary: A low-sidelobe radar codeword seeds later improvements to the minimum-overlap construction.
trajectories.takeaway: The codeword is implemented at iteration 28 without a new best. Reusing the stored source at iteration 30 yields the first subsequent improvement.

trajectories.title: A useful lookup needs more than a citation.
trajectories.summary: The agent consults Lambert-solver documentation, but the added keywords repeat defaults already supplied in the task prompt.
trajectories.takeaway: The two documented revisions do not set a new run best. The record illustrates why retrieving relevant documentation alone does not establish a benefit.

trajectories.title: A published target becomes a starting point.
trajectories.summary: A generated solver combines constrained optimization and radius repair, eventually exceeding the value named in the first query.
trajectories.takeaway: The first query names a published target, but the generated solver still needs numerical optimization and feasibility repair to reach a stronger construction.

trajectories.title: Start from a witness. Then improve it.
trajectories.summary: A second run downloads a published witness and uses it in a program that improves the run’s best score.
trajectories.takeaway: This case explicitly reuses a public construction. Its improvement should be read as artifact reuse followed by optimization, with credit to the original witness.

trajectories.title: Promising evidence. A worse candidate.
trajectories.summary: A retrieval predicted to help precedes a regression. The evaluator preserves the stronger incumbent.
trajectories.takeaway: At iteration 33, the generated child performs worse than its parent. Predicted document scores are hypotheses; the measured result determines what survives.

trajectories.title: A published trajectory, a better final tour.
trajectories.summary: Published seeds, stored implementation details, and further numerical refinement produce a lower-cost Rosetta trajectory.
trajectories.takeaway: Fresh retrieval supplies the reference construction; a later Look-Up resolves its departure-frame convention. The final selected revision proceeds without new retrieval.

programs.title: Routing with fewer SWAPs.
programs.description: A quantum circuit router that combines depth-weighted lookahead, topology-aware scoring, and penalties for reversing recent SWAPs.
programs.note: The improvement is specific to Q20 under the shared evaluator. It is not a claim of superiority on every device topology.

programs.title: Refining an interplanetary journey.
programs.description: A multiple-gravity-assist optimizer that reuses a published Rosetta seed and refines the evaluator-specific trajectory.
programs.note: Published trajectory reuse is part of this result. The orbital plot uses propagated trajectories from the frozen paper data.

programs.title: A finely tuned outer-planet tour.
programs.description: A trajectory search over encounter timing and transfer geometry for the Voyager 2 benchmark.
programs.note: The numerical improvement is small. Both the saved score and reference are displayed at the paper’s precision.

programs.title: Recovering structure in single-cell counts.
programs.description: A denoising program that combines library-size normalization, graph-based smoothing, and count-aware estimates.
programs.note: The headline is the recorded PBMC/Tabula held-out mean. The expression window is a visualization of a PBMC replay, not a new aggregate evaluation.

programs.title: Predicting the effect of a data mixture.
programs.description: A fitted scaling-law program that predicts held-out loss across training-domain mixtures.
programs.note: The figure shows predictions on the frozen held-out data from the paper’s replay.

programs.title: A law for parallel scaling.
programs.description: A fitted scientific model of how loss changes with the benchmark’s parallelism and training variables.
programs.note: The reported score belongs to the archived Gemini-3.8-Flash program at iteration 2.

programs.title: A witness for minimum overlap.
programs.description: A step-function construction that reuses published witness data and applies constrained numerical polishing.
programs.note: The witness comes from public artifacts. The selected program retrieves them at runtime before polishing; the visualization uses the frozen validated replay.

programs.title: An order-29 sign matrix.
programs.description: A search for a 29 × 29 matrix with entries in {−1, +1} and a large absolute determinant.
programs.note: The replay reproduces the recorded exact determinant. Matching the reference score is not proof of a global optimum.

programs.title: More sums, fewer differences.
programs.description: An integer-set search using structured families, exact bitmask scoring, and local refinement.
programs.note: The displayed 509-element set is from the validated replay of this selected N=8 program; it is not the older N=16 construction.

programs.title: 26 circles. One unit square.
programs.description: A variable-radius packing optimized with linearized steps, local exploration, and nonlinear polishing.
programs.note: Circle coordinates are a fresh replay of the archived source. Boundary and pairwise non-overlap constraints were checked.

programs.title: 32 circles, fitted together.
programs.description: A multistart constrained optimizer over staggered layouts, circle centers, and radii.
